facts.statement: The species Eogranivora edentulata was named and described in 2018 by Zheng Xiaoting, Jingmai Kathleen O'Connor, Wang Xiaoli, Wang Yan, and Zhou Zhonghe.
facts.quote: In 2018, the type species Eogranivora edentulata was named and described by Zheng Xiaoting, Jingmai Kathleen O'Connor, Wang Xiaoli, Wang Yan and Zhou Zhonghe.

facts.statement: The generic name refers to the animal being the oldest known seed-eating ornithuromorph bird.
facts.quote: The generic name combines a Greek eos, "dawn", with Neo-Latin granivora, "group of seed eaters", in reference to the species being the oldest known seed-eating ornithuromorph bird.

facts.statement: The specific name means "toothless" in Latin.
facts.quote: The specific name means "toothless" in Latin.

facts.statement: Eogranivora was the first fossil bird species named in 2018.
facts.quote: Eogranivora was the first fossil bird species to have been named in 2018.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen STM35-3 was found in the Yixian Formation dating to about 125 million years ago.
facts.quote: The holotype, STM35-3, was discovered in a layer of the Yixian Formation dating from the early Aptian, at about 125 million years old.

facts.statement: This bird genus lived in present-day China during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Eogranivora is a bird genus, belonging to the Ornithuromorpha, that lived in the area of present-day China during the Early Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Eogranivora is classified as a medium-sized basal ornithuromorph.
facts.quote: Eogranivora is a medium-sized basal ornithuromorph.

facts.statement: Both the upper and lower jaws of Eogranivora are toothless.
facts.quote: Both upper and lower jaws are toothless.

facts.statement: The first metatarsal and first toe are completely missing in this species.
facts.quote: The first metatarsal and the first toe are completely lacking.

facts.statement: Researchers interpret the combination of a seed-filled crop, gastroliths, and a toothless beak as a specialization for eating seeds.
facts.quote: The combination of a crop with seeds—the first time for a Mesozoic ornithuromorph—a mass of small gastroliths and a toothless beak was seen as a specialisation to eat seeds.

facts.statement: The loss of the first toe is hypothesized to be an adaptation for a running lifestyle.
facts.quote: The loss of the first toe would be an adaptation to a running lifestyle.

facts.statement: The time range for this genus is from the Barremian to the Aptian, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)
